# Purpose

This document explains the automated Australian Institute of Petroleum fuel price data pipeline used to collect weekly Diesel and ULP fuel price data and prepare it for Power BI reporting.

The pipeline extracts weekly fuel price series for:

- Darwin
- NT Regional
- NT Average
- National Metropolitan
- National Regional
- National Average

The process is designed to create stable, repeatable outputs for reporting, GitHub storage, and Power BI refresh.

# Pipeline overview

The pipeline follows this process:

1. Open the relevant AIP fuel pricing pages.
2. Read the hidden chart parameters from the page HTML.
3. Use those parameters to call the AIP JSON chart endpoint.
4. Extract the weekly price data from the JSON response.
5. Convert the timestamp and price values into tabular data.
6. Merge all selected series into wide-format Diesel and ULP tables.
7. Export clean CSV files for Power BI.
8. Export a formatted Excel workbook for manual review.
9. Push the output files to GitHub.
10. Connect Power BI to the raw GitHub CSV URLs.

Pipeline flow:

```text
AIP pricing pages
   ↓
Hidden chart parameters
   ↓
AIP JSON chart endpoint
   ↓
Kaggle Python notebook
   ↓
CSV and Excel output files
   ↓
GitHub repository
   ↓
Power BI Web connector
```

# Data source

The data is sourced from the Australian Institute of Petroleum pricing website.

The script does not scrape chart images or manually copy visible numbers. Instead, it opens each AIP pricing page and reads the chart metadata from the HTML element:

```html
<div class="fuel-chart" data-call="..." data-location="...">
```

The key attributes are:

| Attribute | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `data-call` | Identifies the AIP API call to use |
| `data-location` | Identifies the location or series to request |

The script then calls the AIP endpoint:

```text
https://aip.com.au/aip-api-request
```

with parameters similar to:

```text
api-path=public/api
call=<data-call value>
location=<data-location value>
```

The API returns JSON data containing the chart series.

# What is fetched from AIP

The actual fuel price values are fetched from the AIP API.

The API returns each price point in this structure:

```text
[timestamp_in_milliseconds, price_cents_per_litre]
```

Example structure:

```text
[1748786400000, 181.1429]
```

The script converts this into:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Date | Weekly date converted from the timestamp |
| Price | Fuel price in cents per litre |
| Series | The relevant location or average series |

# What is hardcoded

Fuel prices are not hardcoded.

Only these items are manually defined in the script:

- AIP page locations
- Output column names
- Output file names
- GitHub repository settings
- Formatting choices for the Excel workbook

The actual Diesel and ULP prices are fetched directly from the AIP JSON response each time the notebook runs.

The previous manual columns have been removed:

- `Excise Cut (1 Apr)`
- `Fuel Price Lock (20 Apr)`

This keeps the output based only on AIP-returned fuel price data.

## Column definitions

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Date | Date | Full weekly date used for sorting and filtering |
| Week | Text | Short readable week label, such as `4 Jan` |
| Year | Whole number | Calendar year extracted from Date |
| Darwin | Decimal | Darwin fuel price in cents per litre |
| NT Regional | Decimal | NT regional average fuel price in cents per litre |
| NT Average | Decimal | NT average fuel price in cents per litre |
| National Metropolitan | Decimal | National metropolitan average fuel price in cents per litre |
| National Regional | Decimal | National regional average fuel price in cents per litre |
| National Average | Decimal | National average fuel price in cents per litre |

# CSV files

The CSV files are intended for Power BI connection and scheduled refresh.

```text
AIP_diesel_prices.csv
AIP_ulp_prices.csv
```

These files should be used in Power BI through raw GitHub URLs.

# Power BI connection

Power BI should connect to the raw GitHub CSV URLs, not the normal GitHub webpage URLs.

Example Diesel URL:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ResearchTourismNT/Fuel-Prices/main/data/Weekly Fuel Price Data/AIP_diesel_prices.csv
```

Example ULP URL:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ResearchTourismNT/Fuel-Prices/main/data/Weekly Fuel Price Data/AIP_ulp_prices.csv
```

In Power BI:

1. Select **Get Data**.
2. Choose **Web**.
3. Paste the raw GitHub CSV URL.
4. Confirm the preview.
5. Set data types:
   - `Date`: Date
   - `Week`: Text
   - `Year`: Whole number
   - Fuel price columns: Decimal number
6. Load the table.
7. Configure scheduled refresh if required.

# Power BI data type recommendations

| Column | Recommended Power BI type |
|---|---|
| Date | Date |
| Week | Text |
| Year | Whole number |
| Darwin | Decimal number |
| NT Regional | Decimal number |
| NT Average | Decimal number |
| National Metropolitan | Decimal number |
| National Regional | Decimal number |
| National Average | Decimal number |

# Recommended refresh schedule

The AIP data is weekly, so a weekly refresh is usually enough.

Recommended schedule:

```text
Kaggle notebook: Monday morning
GitHub update: Same notebook run
Power BI refresh: After GitHub update
```

A daily refresh can also be used if operationally required, but the source data is weekly, so frequent scraping is generally unnecessary.

# Kaggle setup

The pipeline is intended to run in a Kaggle notebook.

The notebook creates:

- Excel workbook
- Diesel CSV
- ULP CSV
- R Markdown documentation

The notebook then pushes these files to GitHub using a Kaggle secret.

# Kaggle secret

The Kaggle secret must be named exactly:

```text
GITHUB_TOKEN
```

This token should not be pasted directly into the notebook.

# GitHub token setup

Recommended token name:

```text
Kaggle AIP Fuel Prices Bot
```

Recommended token description:

```text
Used by Kaggle notebook to update AIP fuel price CSV and Excel files in ResearchTourismNT/Fuel-Prices for Power BI reporting.
```

Recommended token type:

```text
Fine-grained personal access token
```

Recommended repository access:

```text
Only selected repositories
```

Selected repository:

```text
ResearchTourismNT/Fuel-Prices
```

Required repository permissions:

| Permission | Access |
|---|---|
| Contents | Read and write |
| Metadata | Read |

# GitHub 403 error

If the notebook returns a `403` error when pushing to GitHub, the most likely causes are:

- The token does not have write access.
- The token was created under the wrong resource owner.
- The repository was not selected when creating the token.
- The organisation requires SSO or administrator approval.
- The GitHub user does not have write access to the repository.
- The token has expired.

Recommended fix:

1. Revoke the old token if it was exposed in notebook output.
2. Create a new fine-grained token.
3. Select the correct resource owner.
4. Select the `Fuel-Prices` repository.
5. Set `Contents` to `Read and write`.
6. Save the token in Kaggle as `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
7. Re-run the GitHub push cell.

# Core extraction method

The key extraction logic is:

1. Build possible AIP page URLs.
2. Open the relevant pricing page.
3. Find the chart element.
4. Extract `data-call`.
5. Extract `data-location`.
6. Call the AIP JSON endpoint.
7. Extract `series[0]["data"]`.
8. Convert timestamps to dates.
9. Round prices to one decimal place.
10. Merge all series into a wide table.

# Date conversion

The AIP API returns timestamps in milliseconds.

The script converts these using Python:

```python
pd.to_datetime(timestamp_ms, unit="ms", utc=True)
```

Then it converts the result to the Darwin time zone:

```python
.tz_convert("Australia/Darwin")
```

The final output stores the weekly date as a normal date field.

# Price rounding

The script rounds prices to one decimal place:

```python
round(float(price_cpl), 1)
```

This matches the display style normally used for cents-per-litre fuel prices.

# Validation checks

After each run, the notebook prints a validation summary.

The printed output includes:

- Fuel type being processed
- Column being fetched
- AIP series name
- Number of rows returned
- API call used
- API location used
- Latest Diesel rows
- Latest ULP rows

Recommended checks after each run:

1. Confirm all six series are populated.
2. Confirm Diesel and ULP both have output rows.
3. Confirm the latest Date looks reasonable.
4. Confirm the schema has not changed.
5. Confirm no expected column is fully blank.
6. Confirm GitHub has been updated.
7. Confirm Power BI raw URLs are accessible.

# Data quality considerations

The script only reports data returned by the AIP endpoint.

It does not:

- Invent missing weeks
- Impute missing prices
- Adjust historical values
- Hardcode fuel prices
- Validate prices against a second source

If AIP does not return a value for a given week or series, the output may contain a blank value after merging.

# Troubleshooting AIP extraction

If extraction fails, possible reasons include:

- AIP changed the page URL.
- AIP changed the HTML chart structure.
- The `div.fuel-chart` element is no longer present.
- The `data-call` or `data-location` attributes changed.
- The AIP API endpoint changed.
- The AIP site temporarily failed to respond.

Suggested steps:

1. Open the AIP pricing page manually.
2. Confirm the chart is visible.
3. Re-run the notebook.
4. Check the printed error message.
5. Inspect whether the page still contains `div.fuel-chart`.
6. Update the page definitions if AIP changed a slug.

# Troubleshooting Power BI refresh

If Power BI refresh fails, possible reasons include:

- GitHub raw URL is incorrect.
- GitHub repository is private.
- Power BI credentials need updating.
- CSV file was moved or renamed.
- Column names changed.
- Power Query step refers to an old column.

Suggested steps:

1. Open the raw GitHub URL in a browser.
2. Confirm the CSV downloads or displays.
3. Confirm the file is in the `data/` folder.
4. Confirm the schema is unchanged.
5. Refresh the Power Query preview.
6. Re-apply data types if necessary.
7. Check gateway or credential settings if using a private repository.

# Public versus private GitHub repository

A public repository is simpler for Power BI Web connector refresh because the raw CSV URL is accessible without authentication.

If the repository is private, Power BI may require additional authentication configuration. This can make scheduled refresh more difficult.

# Recommended Power BI modelling approach

Recommended setup:

- Load Diesel and ULP as separate fact tables, or append them into one fact table with a `Fuel Type` column.
- Use `Date` for time-series visuals.
- Use `Year` for slicers.
- Use the six price columns for line charts or comparison visuals.
- If appending Diesel and ULP, reshape the wide table into a long format in Power Query.

Example long-format structure for analysis:

| Date | Week | Year | Fuel Type | Series | Price CPL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-24 | 24 May | 2026 | Diesel | Darwin | 181.1 |
| 2026-05-24 | 24 May | 2026 | ULP | Darwin | 175.2 |

The current CSVs are wide because they match the requested Excel layout.

# Accuracy notes

- Fuel prices are fetched from the AIP JSON endpoint.
- Fuel prices are not hardcoded in the script.
- AIP page locations and output column names are manually defined.
- The pipeline depends on AIP continuing to expose chart data through the same page and API structure.
- The CSV schema should be kept stable to avoid breaking Power BI refreshes.
- The script does not independently verify AIP prices against another source.
- If GitHub is private, Power BI refresh may require additional authentication setup.
- The output should be reviewed after each major change to the script, source website, or Power BI model.
